arun: Quick heads-up: Go SDK starter sample is failing schema_strict checks for fncall outputs when fields are omitted vs null. Repro in sampleapp + logs below. cc @tasha

tasha: Can you paste the payload that fails?

arun: Server returns tool call result with optional field omitted: {"result": {"score": 0.9}} but Go SDK unmarshals into struct with `*string` and sets field to nil. Our client-side schema_strict validator treats nil as JSON null and fails because the schema expects the field to be absent, not null. Error: "expected property 'detail' to be absent, got null"

leo: Ah, classic Go zero-value vs absent problem. JSON null != missing. SDK should distinguish between unset and explicit null when running structured-mode validations.

arun: Workaround for now: change struct tags to `omitempty` and pointer-to-pointer hack, but that's nasty for users.

tasha: Proposed fix: adjust Go SDK's fncall deserializer: when `json_mode=true` and `schema_strict=true`, use raw json.RawMessage for unknown fields and detect `null` vs missing. If field == null -> preserve as JSON null; if missing -> don't include key in reconstructed map before validation. Then run schema validator against that map. Also add doc note about Go pointer semantics.

leo: I'll draft a tiny PR to the Go SDK that uses a two-pass decode: first into map[string]json.RawMessage to see keys, then into typed struct for convenience. Add unit tests for omitted vs null.

ci-bot: CI flaky test: devex/go-sdk-tests 7 test-fncall-null-vs-missing 7 opened DEVEX-4472

arun: Thanks. Please also update starter-kit README with a short note and add a migration snippet. Assigning: leo (PR+tests), tasha (docs).

leo: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/77 (draft)  includes tests. Will request review.

arun: Great — hope this prevents more onboarding friction.
